newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran wants French Middle East role to counter U.S.
newsitem.headline: Iran wants French Middle East role to counter U.S.

text.p: Iran on Wednesday welcomed an active role for France in the Middle East, saying it would counteract U.S. hegemony in the region, the Iranian news agency IRNA reported.
It quoted Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati as saying France's efforts to have an active role in the Middle East were "a positive development in the international scene".
"Efforts of France and other members of the European Union to become involved in Middle East affairs pose obstacles for (the) U.S. monopoly," Velayati said at a news conference.
Velayati was commenting on a tour of the Middle East by French President Jacques Chirac who has been seeking a peacemaking role for Europe alongside the United States.
"The presence of Paris in the region indicates that the European Union has come to its senses and wants to play a role independent of the U.S.," Velayati said.

Iranian media gave wide coverage to an incident in which Chirac protested at Israeli security forces on Tuesday for preventing him from meeting Arabs during a visit to Arab East Jerusalem, captured by Israel in 1967.
Israel later apologised, saying it had been trying to protect Chirac.
Tehran has blasted U.S. policies in the region, saying Washington gives unconditional support to Israel against the Arabs.
Iran says Israel has no right to exist. Tehran has condemned the Middle East peace process, saying it would only lead to a sell-out of Palestinian and Arab rights.
Iran, facing U.S. economic sanctions partly for its opposition to the peace process, has welcomed opposition by EU member states against a U.S. law tightening the sanctions.
